newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Arab ministers adopt anti-terrorism strategy.
newsitem.headline: Arab ministers adopt anti-terrorism strategy.

text.p: Interior ministers from 20 Arab countries on Sunday adopted a strategy to fight "terrorism", a term they generally use to refer to Moslem fundamentalist violence.
The announcement was made in a statement at the end of a two-day meeting in Tunis of the Arab Interior Ministers Council, a specialised body of the Arab League.
The full text of the strategy was not released, but the statement said it constituted a "fundamental and solid base for an efficient cooperation" among the Arab states to fight organised terrorism.

The strategy, which took more than two years of talks to agree, made member states "commit themselves to take effective and firm measures to ban and fight whatever form of terrorism" exists in their county, the council's secretary General Ahmed Assalem told journalists.
The document also calls for close cooperation among member states in investigating and arresting suspects, as well as the freezing of all assets suspected of financing violent acts.

Egyptian Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi, whose country faces armed attacks by Moslem radicals, told the council his country had reports that fundamentalists were against trying to close ranks with the support of unnamed countries.
During the previous years, Algeria and Egypt had accused Iran and Sudan's pro-fundamentalist governments of supporting their own Moslem groups.
